To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is possible to classify 2‐DE gels based on principal component analysis of aligned gels and that principal component analysis of spot volumes makes it possible to investigate protein patterns and to link the patterns to distinct spots for further investigation.
the protein pattern of the wheat varieties could be classified by principal component analysis of spot volume data.

the explorative approach in 2‐DE analysis makes it possible, by using principal components analysis and principal component scores, to screen many 2‐DE gels in order, in a fast, convenient and reliable way, to determine the protein spot patterns that form clusters, and could be selected, for further examination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of explorative data analysis in order to find protein patterns that can be used to classify different wheat varieties.
the use of multivariate data analysis to investigate the variation in protein expression patterns in wheat varieties.

the development of a new approach for classification and analysis of two‐D electrophoresis data, which makes it possible to investigate many samples and to select those samples which are of special interest for further examination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of explorative data analysis in 2‐DE gels makes it easy to screen many gles in order to find clusters of proteins that could be further investigated.
the explorative approach is a valuable tool to screen 2‐D gel data for patterns of interest.
the method is useful to screen a large number of 2‐DE gels in a short time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to analyze 2‐D gel images in a fast, automated way by using explorative data analysis.
the explorative approach to 2‐DE data analysis makes it possible to select a small number of gels for further analysis, which in turn reduces the number of spots to be identified.

the use of principal component analysis, partial least square regression and discriminant analysis on the spot volume lists of the wheat varieties is a good way to classify the gels and to select the proteins that form the basis for differences in protein patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to classify 2‐DE gels in an explorative manner, without prior knowledge of the proteins, by using simple data transformations.
the use of explorative multivariate methods can be used to analyze large numbers of two‐dimension gels in a fast, convenient way.

explorative methods are very useful to find patterns in data, even when the data is not fully understood, and that this can be used in combination with more detailed methods to find the most important patterns.
